title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a stratified space X with strata X_i indexed by a poset I, and Grothendieck's system of tubular neighbourhoods V_i. For a chain (flag) d = (i_0<...<i_n) he writes V_d for the corresponding 'multiple tube'. The neighbourhoods are relative to X' = X*_{I'}. J and L are subsets of I. X'_J is closed, so J is effectively a down-set. X'_L is open, so L is effectively an up-set. The object of study is V_J^L = V_J ∩ X_L^*: the part of the tube around the closed union of strata indexed by J that lies in the open union indexed by L. When J∩L = ∅ this is a deleted (punctured) tubular neighbourhood, i.e. a 'link' region. The margin note says this is the most interesting case.

The previous page wrote V_J^L as a union of the V_{j,l} (j∈J, l∈L, j≤l), with V_{j,j} = V_j. It noted that V_{j,l} ∩ V_{j',l'} is empty unless {j,j',l,l'} is a flag.

(70) lists the possible pairwise intersections, which have at most four indices:
- V_i with i ∈ J∩L;
- V_ij with i∈J, j∈L, i<j;
- V_ijk with i∈J, k∈L, j∈J∪L, i<j<k;
- V_ijkl with i,j∈J, k,l∈L, i<j<k<l.

Grothendieck then abandons gluing pairwise. Instead he takes the full semi-simplicial system closed under intersection.

(71) The pieces are all V_{i_0...i_n} with i_0<...<i_n in J∪L, i_0∈J and i_n∈L.

(72) The arrows are the flag inclusions among such chains. This defines the subposet Drap_J^L(I) ⊂ Drap(J∪L) ⊂ Drap(I) of chains starting in J and ending in L. V_J^L is covered by the V_d, d ∈ Drap_J^L(I), contravariantly in d.

(73) For a sheaf F there is a spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(Drap_J^L(I), d ↦ H^q(V_d,F)) ⇒ H^*(V_J^L,F). Here H^p means the derived limit over the poset.

In modern terms: the link-type space V_J^L is the homotopy colimit, over the poset of chains from J to L, of the elementary multiple tubes V_d. The next page does the same for the 'déploiement' pieces Σ_d, with X = colim over Drap(I) of Σ_d. Purpose: a combinatorial dévissage of the homotopy type and cohomology of neighbourhoods and links in terms of flag-indexed data, as part of the 'déploiement' (unzipping into manifolds-with-corners) programme.
errors: Row 2 of (70) carries an insertion restricting to i ∈ J∖(J∩L) (and j ∈ L∖(J∩L)). The pairwise intersections V_{j,l} actually give V_ij for every i∈J, j∈L with i<j, e.g. i∈J∩L and j∈L. The restriction is unjustified unless meant only to avoid double listing. It is also inconsistent with (71), which imposes no such exclusion.

The list (70) is correct only if J is a down-set and L an up-set (X_J closed, X_L open; cf. 'valable si J<L' on the previous page). Otherwise, for example, flags i<j<k<l with i,k∈J and j,l∈L would also occur.

Drap_J^L(I) is not closed under passing to subflags. A subchain of an admissible chain need not start in J or end in L. So the cover is indexed by a non-face-closed subposet. The spectral sequence (73) then needs the extra observation that, for each point x, the set {d : x∈V_d} is closed under unions of flags, hence has a maximum and is contractible. This holds if V_d ∩ V_d' = V_{d∪d'}, but it is not stated. Topological hypotheses on the cover (open, or closed and locally finite, etc.) are also left implicit.

ideas.what: Covering of V_J ∩ X_L^* (tube of J intersected with open union of L-strata) by multiple tubes V_d indexed by chains d in I with min in J and max in L.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy-colimit / poset-cover decomposition of a (generalized) homotopy link over the chain poset (subdivision) of the stratifying poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Generalized homotopy links indexed by flags: Douteau, Douteau–Waas; décollages over sd(P): Haine (c. 2018–2021); exit paths: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (HA A.6)
ideas.where_published: The flag-indexed dévissage of stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6, tame topology), without these formulas

ideas.what: The poset Drap_J^L(I) of flags starting in J and ending in L.
ideas.modern_name: Interval-type subposet of the barycentric subdivision sd(I) (chains from J to L)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorics; used in stratified homotopy theory (Haine, Douteau)

ideas.what: Spectral sequence H^p(Drap_J^L(I), d ↦ H^q(V_d,F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(V_J^L,F).
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris / descent spectral sequence for a poset-indexed cover (Bousfield–Kan type, derived limits over a poset)
ideas.where_published: Analogous Čech/Leray spectral sequences appear in Tôhoku and SGA 4 (Exposé V)

missed.claim: Grothendieck expresses the cohomology and homotopy type of the 'link' V_J ∩ X_L^* (J∩L = ∅) as a homotopy colimit over chains from J to L of the flag-indexed tubes V_d. This is precisely the shape of the later description of homotopy links in terms of 'generalized homotopy links' HoLink_d, d ∈ sd(P), and of décollages (functors on sd(P)^op) in stratified homotopy theory. The explicit 1981–82 formula for a pair (J,L) of a closed and an open union of strata, via the subposet Drap_J^L, is not credited in that literature.
missed.quote: Drap^L_J(I) ⊂ Drap(J∪L) ⊂ Drap(I) ... drapeaux (i_0…i_n) tels que i_0∈J, i_n∈L ... H^*(V^L_J,F) ⇐ E_2^{pq}=H^p(Drap^L_J(I), d→H^q(V^{X'}_d,F))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, geometrically grounded instance of the décollage / flag-indexed description of stratified spaces (Haine, Douteau–Waas, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping'). It gives a concrete formula for the cohomology of punctured neighbourhoods between unions of strata, useful for priority and historical attribution.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine poset-cover spectral sequence. The interest is that it organizes link-type neighbourhoods by the poset of flags from J to L, anticipating the flag/décollage formalism of modern stratified homotopy theory. Grothendieck's general flag-indexed dévissage idea is, however, already advertised in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Row 2 of (70): the insertion '∖J∩L' is written above the J of 'i ∈ J' (so i ∈ J∖J∩L), followed by 'j ∈ L∖J∩L'. Mathematically, the general condition should be i∈J, j∈L.
Left margin, first note: reads approximately 'NB le cas le plus intéressant est celui où J∩L=∅'.
Left margin, second note: reads approximately 'Et à ce moment, dans les V^{X'}_i ... G pourrait ... il n'y aurait aucun [cas] exclusif'. It is largely illegible; the transcription is uncertain.

Main text before (71): reads approximately 'Il est plus naturel de décrire V_J^L comme la limite inductive des [V_d], ... les morphismes semi-simpliciaux ... dans un système stable par intersection, ... qui pour les V_J^L, on prendra les'.
Line '(72)': the second line reads 'drapeaux (i_0…i_n) qui sont tels que i_0∈J, i_n∈L'.
Last line before (73): 'On aura par ex., pour un faisceau F sur V_J^L'.
